subject: Anthropology
title: Clans and Lineages
description: Learn Clans and Lineages in one minute.

hook.text: A lineage traces every link back to a known ancestor. A clan claims a shared ancestor but can't prove the links.

buildup.text: Lineages are descent groups where every genealogical link is known. Clans share a founding ancestor, often mythical.

discovery.text: Both organize land, marriage rules, and political alliances. They define who you are and where you belong in society.

twist.text: Clan ancestors may be animals, plants, or spirits. The Iroquois Bear clan claims descent from a bear, not a person.

climax.text: Clans and lineages are the backbone of many societies. They organize politics, property, and identity through kinship.

punchline.text: Your ancestor defines your group, real or mythic.

quiz.question: How do clans differ from lineages?
options: Clans claim a shared ancestor but can't prove every genealogical link
Clans are always smaller than lineages

details.summary: Clans are large kin groups claiming descent from a common ancestor, often mythical. Lineages are smaller groups that can trace exact genealogical connections. Both organize social life, regulate marriage, and define political alliances across cultures.
details.whyItMatters: Clans and lineages are the building blocks of social organization in many non-state societies. They determine who can marry, who fights together, who shares land, and who holds authority.
takeaways: Clans claim descent from a common ancestor, often mythical or totemic
Lineages trace exact genealogical connections between members
Both regulate marriage, property rights, and political alliances

faq.question: What is the difference between a clan and a lineage?
faq.answer: A lineage can demonstrate exact genealogical links between members through remembered ancestors. A clan claims common descent but cannot trace the exact connections — the founding ancestor may be mythological, a spirit, or a totem animal.

faq.question: How do clans regulate marriage?
faq.answer: Many clan systems practice exogamy — members must marry outside their own clan. This creates alliances between clans through marriage exchange. Violating clan exogamy rules is considered equivalent to incest in many societies.
